_comment: P11 — CENTAUR_SCOUT (CL6a), status probe-passed.

QUESTION: Does the SEARCH-ARCHITECTURE BRANCH beat the VALIDATED BASELINE at the owner's shape and 2000 ms — and what does the depth ration cost the one-turn search that pays for it? This is the merge decision for claude/cluster-lookahead, not a flag's promotion.
ARMS: baseline  |  search-arch
ARM CONFIGS — A CROSS-BRANCH PAIR: one bundle per arm, from the refs below.
--arm 'baseline=<bundle-baseline>'
--arm 'search-arch=<bundle-search-arch>'
BUNDLES — build one per arm, from the ref named here, and record the
resolved SHA from each bundle.json in findings.md:
tools/simworker/build-bot.sh origin/claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg <bundle-baseline> --fetch
baseline: claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg — baseline
tools/simworker/build-bot.sh origin/claude/cluster-lookahead <bundle-search-arch> --fetch
search-arch: claude/cluster-lookahead — feature
READS OUT: deepestPlies, deepBranches, depthEffectRate, worstWallMs, decisions, score, sharePar

DESIGN NOTE: RESPECIFIED 20260830 AS A BRANCH-VERSUS-BRANCH VALIDATION, under the owner's branching ruling of the same day (docs/BRANCHING.md). THE ARMS ARE TWO BUNDLES FROM TWO REFS, both running their shipped defaults with no bot config on either side: `baseline` is built from origin/claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg, the validated baseline; `search-arch` is built from origin/claude/cluster-lookahead, the search-architecture feature branch, whose default bot carries the deep layer AND the cluster enumeration always-built. WHAT THIS DISSOLVES: the question this row carried until today was 'does the default bot keep carrying two never-raced features, or do they become config fields defaulting off until a sweep promotes them?'. Under the ruling there is no default to argue about — the accumulated architecture lives on a feature branch and the branch either MERGES on this evidence or it does not. The pending owner decision recorded on this row and on CENTAUR_CLUSTER_ENUM's is answered by the paradigm rather than by a status edit. WHAT IT COSTS, SAID OUT LOUD: the previous shape (`default` against `depthless` = bot={"depth":{"plyCap":0}}) was a one-variable pair — same bundle, same evaluator, same bounds, differing only in how far the search could look — and this one is not. Two branch tips differ by everything that landed on either since they forked, so a delta here attributes to THE BRANCH and to nothing finer. That is the correct instrument for a MERGE decision and the wrong one for a mechanism claim, and the two must not be confused in the write-up. The one-variable depth pair remains available on the feature bundle alone and is the follow-up if the branch arm reads positive and somebody wants to know which part of it did the work. AND READ THE RATE FOR WHAT IT IS: the 30% and 22.5% figures on the feature branch are DISAGREEMENT rates — how often removing depth would stage a different move — measured on 11x11 two-team piece boards. They are not improvement and they are not the owner's board; src/lobster/__tests__/DEPTH-NUMBERS.md is the committed record of what each figure measures, and the owner-shape rates (mixed-king 2/24, snake5-queen 5/24) are measured by the `depth-effect rate at the owner's shape` block of src/lobster/__tests__/depth-acceptance.test.ts. Their replay quality signal came back EMPTY — all seven disagreements replay identical same-turn ledgers — which is precisely why this live sweep is the instrument and the probes are not. SIZING, ADDED 20260830: this row now carries a POWER block with a measured block requirement. It is the first experiment in the programme whose size was derived from a measured cross-bundle spread rather than from the 16-block convention, and the convention loses: 16 blocks is about a fifth of what this pair needs.

MERGE DECISION: THIS EXPERIMENT IS THE MERGE DECISION FOR claude/cluster-lookahead. A `search-arch` arm that clears the verified A/A floor on the batch's own metrics merges into claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg and is recorded VALIDATED. An arm that does not clear it does not merge; the branch stays a retained parallel test arm and the reason is written into findings.md. Neither outcome is a status word in this file's schema — the schema judges evidence about flags, and a branch merge is a judgement about a branch — so it is recorded here, in prose, where a reader meets it.

POWER: MEASURED, 20260830, AND IT SAYS 16 BLOCKS CANNOT SETTLE THIS. A sandbox preview ran exactly this pair — baseline 66904d2 against search-arch c74f0a1, both shipped defaults, 8 blocks, potions ON + hazard cross — and returned sharePar -0.01 [-0.31, +0.29]. THE ARM WAS NOT DEAD: 800 scout threads, 370 scout plies and 2,873 cluster joints per game, so the branch ran and decided differently. What it could not do is resolve. Cross-bundle paired spread was +/-0.303 at 8 blocks against an A/A floor of +/-0.10 on the same cells, i.e. THREE TIMES the floor, which cannot tell 'no effect' from 'an effect of 0.3' — the size that would decide the merge either way. Half-width scales as 1/sqrt(blocks), so the arithmetic is 8 x (0.303/0.10)^2 = 73 BLOCKS PER CELL = 219 games per arm per cell = 1,314 games for the spec. THIS SPEC IS EMITTED AT 16 BLOCKS ANYWAY, and that is a budget decision taken with the number in hand rather than an oversight — see REQUIRES for what 16 may and may not claim, and specs/batch2/README.md for what the alternative costs. The 73 is a floor on the blocks, not a target: it buys +/-0.10, which is the smallest effect this instrument can see at all.

PIECE-BEARING CELLS ARE NOT SIZED BY THIS SPEC'S BLOCK COUNT — MEASURED 20260830. An A/A null on a piece-bearing cell, potions ON + hazard cross, TWO IDENTICAL BUNDLES with identical configs and identical seeds, returned sharePar +0.271 [0.037, 0.506] at 8 blocks. IT EXCLUDES ZERO. A cell whose null excludes zero has no floor, and a treatment delta with no floor is UNREADABLE rather than null — the ledger's own rule. All-snake cells at the same size floored cleanly at +/-0.10 (measurements: snakes potions-off +0.041 +/- 0.097, snakes potions-ON hazard -0.093 +/- 0.159 and -0.064 +/- 0.099, against queen potions-ON hazard +0.053 +/- 0.120 on one bundle and +0.271 +/- 0.234 on the other). Carrying the widest measured piece-cell half-width forward, +/-0.234 at 8 blocks, the arithmetic for a +/-0.10 floor is 8 x (0.234/0.10)^2 = 44 BLOCKS PER PIECE CELL. THE CROSSOVER HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED and 44 is an extrapolation from one point, which is why batch 3's rank-2 item is the calibration run that measures it (A/A pairs at 8/16/32/64 blocks on one piece cell, both bundles) rather than a guess repeated at owner-shape prices.

GATE: deepestPlies > 0 and deepBranches > 0 on the `search-arch` arm, on at least the piece-bearing cells. ZERO THERE IS A BROKEN ARM AND MUST BE REPORTED AS A REFUSAL, NOT AS A NULL — it means the bundle was built from the wrong ref, or the deep layer never opened a thread on these boards, and either way the pair measured something other than what it is named for. Record the resolved SHA of both bundles from bundle.json in findings.md: a branch-versus-branch verdict that quotes branch names and not SHAs is a claim nobody can reproduce.

REQUIRES: ONE BUNDLE PER ARM, BUILT FROM THE REF NAMED IN THE BUNDLES BLOCK, AND NO BOT CONFIG ON EITHER. The cross-branch shape is the harness's normal case, not an extension of it: build-bot.sh resolves any git ref to a bundle, and run-pair.js launches the arms at the same instant in separate processes and pairs them afterwards by gameId. Batch 1 ran exactly this shape in P1 — `integrated` @ 66904d2 against `perf-substrate` @ 8059b86, 144 games paired, 0 dropped, 0 pairing problems. DO NOT PASS bot= ON EITHER ARM. The baseline bundle predates the 20260829 flag teardown and has no src/lobster/bot-config module, so checkContenders would REFUSE the spec (correctly) the moment a contender declared one; with no bot config declared, nothing calls requireBundleTakesBotConfig and both arms simply play their shipped bots, which is the comparison this experiment is for. ENGAGEMENT IS READ ON THE search-arch ARM ONLY, from belief.deepestPlies / deepBranches on the per-game rows. The baseline arm is engagement-verified BY CONSTRUCTION — the deep layer is not in that build at all, so there is no counter to read and no silent-A/A risk on that side; the failure mode P5 taught (an arm that names a treatment and quietly does not run it) can only live on the search-arch side, which is where the gate below points.

MINIMUM BLOCKS FOR A CLAIMABLE READ: 73 PER CELL. Below that this spec is a DESCRIPTION, not a merge decision. At the emitted 16 blocks the expected half-width is 0.303 x sqrt(8/16) = about +/-0.21 sharePar, so a 16-block run may report only three things and must report them in these words: (1) THE ENGAGEMENT GATE below, which is a real pass/fail at any block count and is the single most valuable thing 16 blocks buys; (2) the mechanism rows — deepestPlies, deepBranches, depthEffectRate, worstWallMs, decisions — which are per-decision counts rather than per-game outcomes and are readable at this size; (3) a sharePar interval quoted WITH its half-width and labelled UNDERPOWERED FOR THE MERGE DECISION. A null at 16 blocks is NOT evidence the branch does not help and must never be written as one, because an effect of +0.2 sharePar would sit inside that interval. THE MERGE MAY NOT BE DECIDED — in either direction — ON A 16-BLOCK RUN. If the night has room for 73 blocks on even ONE cell, run the one cell at 73 rather than three cells at 16: one cell that can answer the question beats three that cannot.

MINIMUM BLOCKS FOR A CLAIMABLE READ ON A PIECE-BEARING CELL: 44, and this spec is emitted at 16. Blocks are a property of the SPEC and not of a cell (the standing CELL-QUALITY open item), so a piece cell cannot be raised without raising the all-snake cell beside it and the mandatory A/A null with it. Until the calibration lands, read this spec's PIECE cells (hazard-mix-king, headline-mix-king) under one rule: A DELTA ON A PIECE CELL IS QUOTED ONLY AGAINST N0's FLOOR MEASURED ON THAT SAME CELL, ON THE SAME BUNDLE, AT THE SAME BLOCK COUNT — and if that floor does not contain zero, the cell reports UNREADABLE and no verdict is written from it. The all-snake cells in this spec are unaffected and floor at +/-0.10. This is not a reason to skip the spec: its mechanism rows are per-decision counts, they are readable at this size, and they are what most of these experiments were designed to read.
HOW AN ARM IS SELECTED HERE, AND WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT. This is a
BRANCH-VERSUS-BRANCH pair under the branching paradigm (docs/BRANCHING.md,
owner ruling 20260830): an architecture change is built on its own branch,
validated as a batch arm, and MERGED on the result. So the arms are two
BUNDLES built from two refs, each running its own shipped default, and the
BUNDLES block above is the whole of the arm definition.
DO NOT ADD bot= TO EITHER ARM unless this spec prints one. A bundle built
from a pre-teardown ref has no src/lobster/bot-config module, and
checkContenders refuses a spec that declares a bot config against it —
correctly, because such a bundle would ignore the config and play its
shipped bot under the arm's name. With no config declared, that check does
not fire and both arms simply play what they ship, which is the comparison.
READ THE VERDICT AT THE RIGHT GRAIN. Two branch tips differ by everything
that landed on either since they forked, so a delta attributes to THE
BRANCH and to nothing finer. That is the right instrument for a merge
decision and the wrong one for a mechanism claim.
